questions.subject: Pediatrics

options.label: A
options.explanation: Anterior horn cell destruction is patchy, giving an asymmetrical, flaccid, predominantly proximal lower motor neuron paralysis.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Polio affects only motor neurons of the anterior horn; sensation is characteristically preserved, which helps distinguish it from GBS.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Sphincters are usually spared in poliomyelitis; early bladder involvement points towards transverse myelitis or cord compression.

options.label: D
options.explanation: CSF shows a lymphocytic pleocytosis with normal or only marginally raised protein; marked protein rise with few cells suggests GBS instead.

questions.pearl: Acute flaccid paralysis: asymmetric, sensation intact, no sphincter loss = polio; symmetric ascending with albuminocytological dissociation = GBS.

questions.subject: Pediatrics
questions.stem: Vaccines in the EPI schedule of Bangladesh:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Rabies vaccine is given as post-exposure (or high-risk pre-exposure) prophylaxis, not as part of routine childhood EPI.

options.label: B
options.explanation: BCG is given at birth (or first contact) intradermally over the left deltoid to protect against severe childhood TB.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Oral cholera vaccine is used in outbreak or high-risk campaigns but is not in the routine EPI schedule.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Hepatitis B is given within the pentavalent vaccine (DPT-HepB-Hib) at 6, 10 and 14 weeks.

questions.pearl: Bangladesh EPI covers BCG, pentavalent, PCV, OPV/IPV, MR and TT/Td; pentavalent = DPT + Hep B + Hib.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Dental pain, especially an impacted lower third molar, is referred to the ear via the mandibular branch of the trigeminal nerve (auriculotemporal).

options.label: B
options.explanation: Adenoids cause ear symptoms by Eustachian tube obstruction (otitis media with effusion), a true middle ear problem rather than referred pain.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Pain from the tonsil travels via the glossopharyngeal nerve (tympanic branch, Jacobson's nerve), so tonsillitis and post-tonsillectomy pain are referred to the ear.

options.label: D
options.explanation: TMJ arthritis or dysfunction is a very common cause of otalgia with a normal ear, via the auriculotemporal nerve.

questions.pearl: Referred otalgia nerves: V, VII, IX, X and C2/C3 — think teeth, TMJ, tonsil, larynx, cervical spine; always examine the larynx in an adult.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Brawny swelling of the floor of the mouth pushes the tongue up and back, causing painful dysphagia and drooling.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Spread to the parapharyngeal space and laryngeal oedema can obstruct the airway; stridor signals impending airway compromise requiring urgent control.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Involvement of the pterygoid muscles and submandibular space produces trismus.

options.label: D
options.text: Incision and drainage is the treatment of choice
options.explanation: First-line treatment is airway protection and high-dose IV antibiotics; surgical decompression is reserved for non-response or abscess formation.

questions.pearl: Ludwig's angina is a bilateral submandibular space cellulitis, usually from the lower second/third molars; the airway is the main threat.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Fever is a minor Jones criterion.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Migratory polyarthritis of large joints is a major criterion and the most common major manifestation.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Raised ESR or CRP is a minor criterion (acute phase reactant).

options.label: D
options.explanation: Sydenham's chorea is a major criterion and can appear late, even as the sole manifestation.

questions.pearl: Major Jones criteria (CASES): Carditis, Arthritis, Subcutaneous nodules, Erythema marginatum, Sydenham's chorea.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: COPD causes ventilation-perfusion mismatch and alveolar hypoventilation, giving hypoxia with hypercapnia (PaCO2 > 6 kPa).

options.label: B
options.explanation: Pneumonia typically produces type 1 failure (hypoxia with normal or low PaCO2) through V/Q mismatch and shunting.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Respiratory muscle weakness in Guillain-Barré syndrome causes pump failure and hypoventilation, giving type 2 failure.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Paradoxical chest wall movement and pain reduce effective ventilation, leading to CO2 retention.

questions.pearl: Type 2 failure = pump problem (COPD, neuromuscular disease, chest wall deformity, sedative overdose); type 1 = lung parenchyma/V/Q problem.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Lipophilic agents such as propranolol cross the blood-brain barrier and can cause depression, nightmares and fatigue.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Non-selective beta blockers raise triglycerides and lower HDL cholesterol.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Erectile dysfunction is a recognised adverse effect and a common reason for non-adherence.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Beta-2 blockade causes bronchoconstriction, so non-selective agents are contraindicated in asthma.

questions.pearl: Beta blocker adverse effects: bradycardia, heart block, bronchospasm, cold peripheries, masked hypoglycaemia, fatigue, nightmares.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Decompensated cirrhosis with hepatic encephalopathy produces asterixis, a negative myoclonus from a metabolic brain disturbance.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Hepatomegaly alone does not cause asterixis; it needs liver failure with encephalopathy.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Uraemic encephalopathy in advanced renal failure is a classic cause of flapping tremor.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Meningitis causes fever, neck stiffness and altered consciousness but not asterixis.

questions.pearl: Asterixis causes: hepatic encephalopathy, uraemia, CO2 retention (type 2 respiratory failure) and other metabolic encephalopathies.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Dysmetria on finger-nose testing (past pointing) is a hallmark of cerebellar incoordination.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Athetosis is a slow writhing movement from basal ganglia (striatal) disease, not the cerebellum.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Resting tremor is extrapyramidal (Parkinson's); cerebellar disease gives an intention tremor.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Cerebellar lesions cause scanning (staccato) dysarthria from incoordination of the speech muscles, a classic cerebellar sign.

questions.pearl: Cerebellar signs (DANISH): Dysdiadochokinesia, Ataxia, Nystagmus, Intention tremor, Scanning dysarthria, Hypotonia.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Failure to excrete H+ and regenerate bicarbonate, with retained phosphate and sulphate, produces a high anion gap acidosis.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Cortisol excess has mineralocorticoid effects, causing hypokalaemic metabolic alkalosis.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Loss of bicarbonate-rich intestinal fluid causes a normal anion gap (hyperchloraemic) acidosis.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Severe falciparum malaria causes lactic acidosis from tissue hypoxia and parasite glycolysis; it is a marker of poor prognosis.

questions.pearl: High anion gap acidosis (MUDPILES): Methanol, Uraemia, DKA, Paraldehyde, Iron/INH, Lactate, Ethylene glycol, Salicylates.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Hypokalaemia flattens and may invert the T wave, with ST depression.

options.label: B
options.explanation: QRS widening is a feature of severe hyperkalaemia rather than hypokalaemia.

options.label: C
options.explanation: A prominent U wave (with apparent long QT, really QU) is the classic sign of hypokalaemia.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Loss of P waves is seen in hyperkalaemia; hypokalaemia tends to increase P wave amplitude.

questions.pearl: Hypokalaemia ECG: flat/inverted T, ST depression, prominent U wave, prolonged QU; hyperkalaemia: tall tented T, flat P, wide QRS, sine wave.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Calcium gluconate (or chloride) is used for membrane stabilisation; calcium oxalate is a kidney stone constituent, not a drug.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Insulin drives K+ into cells via Na+/K+-ATPase; glucose is given with it to prevent hypoglycaemia.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Nebulised beta-2 agonists shift potassium intracellularly, lowering serum K+ by about 0.5–1 mmol/L.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Beta blockers impair cellular K+ uptake and can worsen hyperkalaemia.

questions.pearl: Hyperkalaemia: stabilise (calcium gluconate), shift (insulin-glucose, salbutamol, bicarbonate), remove (resonium, diuretics, dialysis).

questions.subject: Obstetrics

options.label: A
options.explanation: A persistent brow presents the mentovertical diameter (13.5 cm), which cannot pass a normal pelvis.

options.label: B
options.explanation: A scarred or rigid cervix fails to dilate despite good contractions, obstructing descent.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The gynaecoid pelvis is the normal, most favourable pelvis for vaginal delivery.

options.label: D
options.explanation: An ovarian tumour impacted in the pouch of Douglas acts as a pelvic tumour obstructing the birth canal.

questions.pearl: Obstructed labour causes: passage (contracted pelvis, pelvic tumours, cervical dystocia) and passenger (malpresentation, big baby, hydrocephalus).

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis causes clubbing in about two-thirds of patients.

options.label: B
options.explanation: COPD does not cause clubbing; its presence in a COPD patient should prompt a search for lung cancer or bronchiectasis.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Asthma, however severe, does not cause clubbing.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Chronic suppurative lung disease such as bronchiectasis is a classic cause of clubbing.

questions.pearl: Respiratory clubbing: lung cancer, suppurative lung disease (bronchiectasis, abscess, empyema, CF), fibrosing alveolitis, asbestosis — never COPD or asthma.

questions.subject: Pediatrics

options.label: A
options.explanation: Measles involves the brain parenchyma (encephalitis) rather than causing a meningitis.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Acute post-infectious encephalitis occurs in about 1 in 1000 cases; SSPE is a late complication.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Measles keratitis, especially with vitamin A deficiency, leads to corneal ulceration and keratomalacia — a major cause of childhood blindness.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Severe measles-associated diarrhoea with dehydration can cause prerenal acute kidney injury in malnourished children.

questions.pearl: Commonest measles complication is pneumonia (commonest cause of death); give vitamin A to all children with measles.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Effusion gives stony dullness; woody dullness is the descriptor for consolidation or fibrosis.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Blunting of the costophrenic angle on chest X-ray appears once about 200–300 mL of fluid collects.

options.label: C
options.explanation: A large effusion pushes the mediastinum and trachea away from the affected side.

options.label: D
options.text: Breath sound diminished on opposite side
options.explanation: Breath sounds are diminished or absent on the same side as the effusion.

questions.pearl: Pleural effusion: reduced expansion, stony dull percussion, reduced breath sounds and vocal resonance, trachea away if large.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: The classic gut complications are perforation and haemorrhage from ulcerated Peyer's patches, not obstruction.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Salmonella can cause acute cholecystitis and chronic carriage in a diseased gallbladder, but gallstones themselves are not a complication.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Salmonella osteomyelitis is a recognised complication, especially in sickle cell disease.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Metastatic focal infection, including psoas abscess, can follow typhoid bacteraemia.

questions.pearl: Typhoid perforation typically occurs in the third week, in the terminal ileum (antimesenteric border over Peyer's patches).

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.stem: Causes of a red mass in the nose:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Rhinosporidium seeberi produces a friable, strawberry-like red polypoidal mass studded with white spots that bleeds easily.

options.label: B
options.explanation: A hypertrophied turbinate is a firm, congested mucosal swelling that shrinks with decongestant, not a red mass lesion.

options.label: C
options.explanation: A deviated nasal septum is a deformity of the septum covered with normal mucosa, not a mass.

options.label: D
options.explanation: A bleeding polypus of the septum (capillary haemangioma) presents as a red polypoid mass; ordinary ethmoidal polyps are pale grey.

questions.pearl: Red nasal masses: rhinosporidiosis, bleeding polypus of septum, angiofibroma (adolescent male); pale masses: ethmoidal and antrochoanal polyps.

questions.subject: Pediatrics
questions.stem: Treatment of cerebral malaria in children:

options.label: A
options.explanation: IV quinine remains an effective alternative when artesunate is unavailable, given with glucose monitoring for hypoglycaemia.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Parenteral artesunate is the drug of choice for severe malaria in children and adults, with lower mortality than quinine.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Widespread P. falciparum resistance makes chloroquine unsuitable for severe falciparum malaria.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Primaquine is a gametocytocide and hypnozoiticide; it has no role in treating severe malaria.

questions.pearl: Severe malaria: IV artesunate 2.4 mg/kg at 0, 12, 24 h then daily, followed by a full oral ACT course.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences
questions.stem: Parasites that infect by penetrating the skin:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Filariform larvae of hookworm penetrate intact skin, usually of the feet, causing ground itch.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The New World hookworm also enters by skin penetration of filariform larvae.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Cercariae penetrate skin in fresh water, sometimes causing swimmer's itch.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Beef tapeworm is acquired by eating undercooked beef containing cysticerci.

questions.pearl: Skin-penetrating helminths: hookworms, Strongyloides and Schistosoma cercariae.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Thyroid hormone increases atrial automaticity and shortens refractoriness; check TSH in every new AF.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Acute myocardial infarction causes AF through atrial ischaemia, stretch and heart failure.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Binge drinking triggers AF ('holiday heart'), and chronic use causes alcoholic cardiomyopathy.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Hypopituitarism causes secondary hypothyroidism and adrenal insufficiency, which slow rather than provoke AF.

questions.pearl: Common AF causes: hypertension, IHD, rheumatic mitral valve disease, thyrotoxicosis, alcohol, heart failure, pneumonia, PE.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Inflamed bronchial mucosa may cause blood streaking of sputum; it is the commonest cause of minor haemoptysis.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Thrombocytopenia and leukaemic infiltration or infection can cause pulmonary bleeding and haemoptysis.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Erosion of vessels in the abscess wall produces haemoptysis with foul purulent sputum.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Raised pulmonary venous pressure ruptures bronchial veins (pulmonary apoplexy) or causes pink frothy sputum in pulmonary oedema.

questions.pearl: In Bangladesh, always exclude pulmonary tuberculosis in haemoptysis; other big causes are bronchiectasis and bronchogenic carcinoma.

questions.subject: Pediatrics

options.label: A
options.explanation: A mid-upper arm circumference below 115 mm in a child 6–59 months defines SAM.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Jaundice is not a defining feature of SAM.

options.label: C
options.explanation: SAM is defined by weight-for-height Z score below -3 SD; above -3 does not meet the criterion.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Bilateral pitting pedal oedema (nutritional oedema/kwashiorkor) defines SAM regardless of anthropometry.

questions.pearl: WHO SAM criteria (6–59 months): WHZ < -3, MUAC < 115 mm, or bilateral pitting oedema — any one is enough.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Preformed heat-stable enterotoxin causes vomiting within 1–6 hours of eating contaminated food; it is a classic food poisoning organism.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Enterotoxigenic and enterohaemorrhagic E. coli cause food-borne diarrhoeal disease.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Staph. epidermidis is a skin commensal causing device-related infections; it does not produce enterotoxin.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Preformed neurotoxin in canned or preserved food causes botulism, a form of food poisoning with descending paralysis.

questions.pearl: Short-incubation (1–6 h) vomiting: Staph. aureus and Bacillus cereus toxins; longer incubation: Salmonella, C. perfringens.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Raised portal pressure causes congestive splenomegaly, often with hypersplenism.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Testicular atrophy is a feature of hepatocellular failure (oestrogen excess), not of portal hypertension itself.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Sinusoidal hypertension, with hypoalbuminaemia and sodium retention, drives ascites.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Recanalised paraumbilical veins form dilated periumbilical collaterals radiating from the umbilicus.

questions.pearl: Portal hypertension = portal pressure > 10 mmHg; varices bleed when HVPG exceeds 12 mmHg.

questions.subject: Pediatrics
questions.stem: IV fluids used in severe dehydration due to diarrhoea:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Cholera saline (Dhaka solution) replaces sodium, potassium and bicarbonate (as acetate) losses and is the standard IV fluid in Bangladesh.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Normal saline corrects volume but supplies no potassium or base, so acidosis and hypokalaemia persist; it is only a second-line option.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Ringer's lactate (Hartmann) is the WHO-recommended IV fluid for plan C when cholera saline is unavailable.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Plasmasol is a plasma volume expander for haemorrhagic or surgical shock, not the fluid of choice for diarrhoeal dehydration.

questions.pearl: WHO Plan C: 100 mL/kg Ringer's lactate — infants over 6 h (30 mL/kg in 1 h), older children over 3 h (30 mL/kg in 30 min).

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Constriction impairs right heart filling, giving a raised JVP with Kussmaul's sign and a prominent y descent.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Isolated left heart failure raises pulmonary venous pressure; the JVP rises only when the right heart fails.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Pulmonary tuberculosis itself does not raise the JVP unless complicated by constrictive pericarditis or cor pulmonale.

options.label: D
options.explanation: There is no such lesion; tricuspid stenosis, not 'atrial stenosis', gives a raised JVP with giant a waves.

questions.pearl: Raised JVP with a non-pulsatile, non-filling column suggests SVC obstruction.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Cystic fibrosis (CFTR mutation) is autosomal recessive.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Haemophilia A is X-linked recessive.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Marfan syndrome results from autosomal dominant fibrillin-1 mutations.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Most hereditary spherocytosis (ankyrin, spectrin defects) is inherited as autosomal dominant.

questions.pearl: Autosomal dominant examples: Marfan, ADPKD, hereditary spherocytosis, FAP, NF1, Huntington's, familial hypercholesterolaemia, von Willebrand disease (most types).

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Parasitised red cells rupture at schizogony and are removed by the spleen; blackwater fever is massive intravascular haemolysis.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Viral hepatitis causes hepatocellular jaundice, not haemolysis.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Ineffective erythropoiesis and haemolysis of abnormal red cells cause chronic haemolytic anaemia.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Primary biliary cholangitis causes cholestatic jaundice from autoimmune destruction of small bile ducts.

questions.pearl: Haemolysis: raised unconjugated bilirubin, raised LDH, reticulocytosis, low haptoglobin, urinary urobilinogen but no bilirubinuria.

questions.subject: Obstetrics

options.label: A
options.explanation: Prolonged labour with exhaustion and dehydration leads to ketoacidosis in the mother.

options.label: B
options.explanation: An exhausted uterus becomes atonic after delivery, and genital tract trauma adds to bleeding.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Antepartum haemorrhage occurs before labour and is not a consequence of obstruction.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Continued contractions against obstruction thin the lower segment (Bandl's ring) until it ruptures, especially in multiparae.

questions.pearl: Late maternal sequelae of obstructed labour include vesicovaginal fistula from pressure necrosis of the bladder base.

questions.subject: Specialized Surgery
questions.stem: Biochemical changes in gastric outlet obstruction:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Vomiting loses sodium; with water intake the result is hyponatraemia.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Renal potassium loss from secondary hyperaldosteronism and bicarbonaturia causes hypokalaemia.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Loss of HCl causes hypochloraemic metabolic alkalosis.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Alkalosis lowers ionised calcium, which may cause tetany; calcium is not raised.

questions.pearl: Pyloric stenosis picture: hypochloraemic, hypokalaemic metabolic alkalosis with paradoxical aciduria; correct with 0.9% saline plus KCl.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Viral hepatitis, particularly hepatitis A, can run a prolonged cholestatic phase with an obstructive biochemical picture.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Autoimmune destruction of intrahepatic bile ducts causes intrahepatic cholestasis with itch and raised ALP.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Viperine venom causes haemolysis (prehepatic jaundice), not biliary obstruction.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Sickle cell anaemia causes haemolytic jaundice; pigment stones may complicate it but the anaemia itself is prehepatic.

questions.pearl: Cholestasis pattern: high conjugated bilirubin, ALP and GGT, pale stools, dark urine with bilirubin, pruritus.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Peritubular interstitial fibroblasts secrete erythropoietin in response to hypoxia.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Renal medulla produces PGE2 and PGI2, which maintain renal blood flow, especially when perfusion falls.

options.label: C
options.explanation: ADH is synthesised in the hypothalamus (supraoptic and paraventricular nuclei) and released from the posterior pituitary.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Epinephrine is produced by the adrenal medulla, not the kidney.

questions.pearl: Kidney endocrine products: erythropoietin, renin, calcitriol (1-alpha hydroxylation), prostaglandins, kinins.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: Signs of upper motor neuron lesion:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Marked wasting is a lower motor neuron sign; UMN lesions give only mild disuse atrophy.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Loss of descending inhibition causes spasticity (clasp-knife) with weakness in a pyramidal pattern.

options.label: C
options.explanation: UMN lesions give an extensor plantar (Babinski) response.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Tone is increased in established UMN lesions; hypotonia is an LMN or cerebellar sign (or acute spinal shock).

questions.pearl: UMN: spasticity, hyperreflexia, clonus, extensor plantar, pyramidal weakness; LMN: wasting, fasciculation, hypotonia, areflexia.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Retroauricular pain often precedes or accompanies the onset of facial weakness.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Bell's palsy is an LMN facial nerve palsy, so the forehead is also involved.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Involvement of the nerve proximal to the chorda tympani causes loss of taste on the anterior two-thirds of the tongue.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Facial sensation is carried by the trigeminal nerve and is preserved; patients may report subjective numbness only.

questions.pearl: Bell's palsy: prednisolone within 72 hours improves recovery; protect the eye. About 80% recover fully.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.stem: Indications of blood transfusion in surgical patients:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Severe haemolysis with symptomatic anaemia or haemolytic disease of the newborn may require transfusion or exchange transfusion.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Symptomatic chronic anaemia before urgent surgery, with no time for correction, is an indication for transfusion.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Severe iron deficiency anaemia needing urgent surgery or with cardiac decompensation may need preoperative transfusion.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Polycythaemia needs venesection, not transfusion; adding red cells would worsen hyperviscosity.

questions.pearl: Restrictive transfusion threshold: Hb 7 g/dL in most stable patients (8 g/dL with cardiovascular disease).

questions.subject: Basic Sciences
questions.stem: Factors that increase transmembrane potassium influx into cells:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Beta blockade reduces Na+/K+-ATPase stimulation and so impairs cellular K+ uptake; beta-2 agonists increase it.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Glucagon does not promote cellular K+ uptake; it can mildly raise plasma K+ through hepatic release.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Insulin stimulates Na+/K+-ATPase, driving K+ into cells — the basis of insulin-glucose therapy in hyperkalaemia.

options.label: D
options.explanation: In acidosis H+ enters cells in exchange for K+, which moves out and raises plasma potassium; alkalosis does the opposite.

questions.pearl: Shift of K+ into cells: insulin, beta-2 agonists, alkalosis, aldosterone; out of cells: acidosis, cell lysis, beta blockade, hyperosmolality.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Ceftriaxone is a beta-lactam that inhibits cell wall synthesis, not protein synthesis.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Beta-lactams bind penicillin-binding proteins (transpeptidases), blocking peptidoglycan cross-linking.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Cross-reactivity with penicillin allergy is low with third-generation cephalosporins, so serious hypersensitivity is less frequent than with penicillins.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Ceftriaxone is a third-generation cephalosporin; cefepime is fourth generation.

questions.pearl: Ceftriaxone: long half-life (once daily), biliary excretion (no renal dose change), may cause biliary sludge; avoid with calcium IV in neonates.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences
questions.stem: Which of these are produced by the kidney:

options.label: A
options.explanation: ADH comes from hypothalamic neurons and is stored in the posterior pituitary; the kidney is its target, not its source.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Immunoglobulins are secreted by plasma cells of the lymphoid system.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The kidney synthesises vasodilator prostaglandins that protect renal perfusion; NSAIDs block these.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Renal peritubular cells produce about 90% of erythropoietin, so CKD causes normocytic anaemia.

questions.pearl: NSAIDs can precipitate AKI in volume-depleted patients by blocking renal prostaglandin-mediated afferent arteriolar dilatation.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Loss of negative feedback from low thyroid hormone raises TSH, the most sensitive test for primary hypothyroidism.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Free T4 is low in hypothyroidism.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Free T3 is low or low-normal; it is a poor test for hypothyroidism.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Hashimoto's thyroiditis, the commonest cause in iodine-sufficient areas, is marked by anti-TPO antibodies.

questions.pearl: Subclinical hypothyroidism: raised TSH with normal FT4; positive TPO antibodies predict progression to overt disease.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.stem: Nerves that can be injured in total thyroidectomy:

options.label: A
options.explanation: The recurrent laryngeal nerve lies in the tracheo-oesophageal groove close to the inferior thyroid artery; injury causes hoarseness or bilateral cord palsy.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The internal laryngeal nerve pierces the thyrohyoid membrane well above the thyroid gland and is rarely at risk.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The external laryngeal nerve runs with the superior thyroid artery and can be injured while ligating the upper pole, weakening the cricothyroid (voice pitch).

options.label: D
options.explanation: The phrenic nerve lies on scalenus anterior, deep to the prevertebral fascia, outside the field of thyroidectomy.

questions.pearl: Ligate the superior thyroid artery close to the gland (protects external laryngeal nerve) and the inferior thyroid artery away from it (protects recurrent laryngeal nerve).

questions.subject: Obstetrics

options.label: A
options.explanation: Heavy proteinuria (5 g or more in 24 hours in older definitions) reflects severe glomerular endotheliosis.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Pre-eclampsia is a hypertensive disorder; severe disease has BP of 160/110 mmHg or more.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Onset of seizures defines eclampsia, a separate (more advanced) diagnosis rather than a feature of pre-eclampsia.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Haemolysis, elevated liver enzymes and low platelets is a severe feature of pre-eclampsia.

questions.pearl: Severe features: BP 160/110 or more, thrombocytopenia, raised transaminases, renal impairment, pulmonary oedema, headache, visual disturbance.

questions.subject: Gynecology

options.label: A
options.explanation: Combined pills suppress lactation and raise the thrombosis risk early postpartum, so they are avoided in breastfeeding women for the first 6 months.

options.label: B
options.explanation: A copper IUD can be inserted within 48 hours of delivery or after 4–6 weeks and does not affect breastfeeding.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The progestogen-only pill does not reduce milk output and is ideal for lactating mothers.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Condoms are safe at any time postpartum and add STI protection.

questions.pearl: Lactational amenorrhoea method is reliable only if exclusively breastfeeding, amenorrhoeic and less than 6 months postpartum.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Hypoxia-driven hyperventilation in pneumonia usually causes respiratory alkalosis, unless the patient is exhausted.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Acute asthma typically lowers PaCO2; a normal or rising PaCO2 is a life-threatening sign rather than the usual pattern.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Chronic alveolar hypoventilation causes CO2 retention, giving respiratory acidosis with renal bicarbonate compensation.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Diarrhoea causes metabolic (normal anion gap) acidosis from bicarbonate loss.

questions.pearl: Respiratory acidosis = hypoventilation: COPD, opioid overdose, neuromuscular weakness, chest wall disease, obesity hypoventilation.

questions.subject: Gynecology

options.label: A
options.explanation: Combined pills are an ideal reversible method for young nulliparous women without contraindications.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Nulliparity is traditionally a relative contraindication to IUCD (higher expulsion, pain and PID concern), so it is not the first choice.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The etonogestrel implant has no parity restriction and is one of the most effective reversible methods.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Progestogen-only pills can be used by nulliparous women, especially when oestrogen is contraindicated.

questions.pearl: Ideal contraceptive for a newly married nulliparous woman: combined oral contraceptive pill.

questions.subject: Gynecology

options.label: A
options.explanation: Gonococcal urethritis is by definition excluded from non-gonococcal urethritis.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Chlamydia (serovars D–K) is the commonest cause of NGU.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Staph. aureus is not a recognised cause of sexually transmitted urethritis.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Genital mycoplasmas (M. genitalium, M. hominis) and Ureaplasma cause NGU.

questions.pearl: NGU treatment: doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 7 days (or single-dose azithromycin); treat partners.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Prednisone is an oral prodrug converted to prednisolone in the liver.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Hydrocortisone is used IV in acute severe asthma and adrenal crisis, not by inhalation.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Beclomethasone dipropionate is a standard inhaled corticosteroid for asthma prophylaxis.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Fluticasone is a potent inhaled corticosteroid with high first-pass metabolism.

questions.pearl: Inhaled steroids: beclomethasone, budesonide, fluticasone, ciclesonide, mometasone; rinse the mouth to prevent oral candidiasis.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Pulmonary vein thrombi would embolise to the systemic circulation, not to the pulmonary arteries.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Calf vein DVT can propagate proximally and embolise; deep veins of the leg are the main source of PE.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Pelvic vein thrombosis (post-partum, pelvic surgery) is an important source of pulmonary emboli.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Left heart thrombi (e.g. LV aneurysm, AF) cause systemic emboli such as stroke, not PE.

questions.pearl: Most PEs arise from proximal (iliofemoral) DVT; isolated calf DVT carries a lower risk unless it propagates.

questions.subject: Pediatrics

options.label: A
options.explanation: Chronic hypoxaemia stimulates erythropoietin, causing secondary polycythaemia and risk of cerebral thrombosis.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Pulmonary blood flow is reduced in TOF, so recurrent chest infection is not a feature (unlike left-to-right shunts).

options.label: C
options.explanation: Ventricular arrhythmias and sudden death occur, particularly after surgical repair.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Pulmonary regurgitation is the commonest long-term complication after repair with transannular patching.

questions.pearl: Unrepaired TOF complications: hypercyanotic spells, cerebral thrombosis, brain abscess, infective endocarditis, polycythaemia.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Cystic hygroma is a lymphatic malformation typically in the posterior triangle, lateral in position.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Sublingual (submental) dermoid cysts arise in the midline from trapped ectoderm.

options.label: C
options.explanation: It arises along the thyroglossal tract in the midline and moves upward on protrusion of the tongue.

options.label: D
options.explanation: A branchial cyst lies laterally at the anterior border of sternocleidomastoid at the junction of its upper and middle thirds.

questions.pearl: Midline neck swellings: thyroglossal cyst, isthmus thyroid nodule, submental lymph node, dermoid, subhyoid bursa, plunging ranula.

questions.subject: Specialized Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Anorectal malformations are uncommon, about 1 in 4000–5000 live births.

options.label: B
options.explanation: In high (supralevator) lesions the rectum ends above the levator ani, often with a fistula to the urinary tract.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Low lesions include covered anus, anal stenosis and anocutaneous fistula, with the bowel passing through the levator.

options.label: D
options.explanation: High lesions need an initial colostomy followed by posterior sagittal anorectoplasty; low lesions may need only perineal surgery.

questions.pearl: Always examine for associated VACTERL anomalies (vertebral, anorectal, cardiac, TOF, renal, limb) in imperforate anus.

questions.subject: Obstetrics
questions.stem: Causes of antepartum haemorrhage in multiple pregnancy:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Atony causes postpartum haemorrhage, not antepartum haemorrhage.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Overdistension, hypertension and sudden decompression after delivery of the first twin increase abruption.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The large placental surface area in multiple pregnancy extends into the lower segment more often.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Coagulopathy is not a recognised specific cause of APH in multiple pregnancy.

questions.pearl: Multiple pregnancy raises the risk of anaemia, pre-eclampsia, polyhydramnios, preterm labour, APH and PPH.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Haemophilia A is factor VIII deficiency; haemophilia B (Christmas disease) is factor IX deficiency.

options.label: B
options.explanation: As an X-linked recessive disorder, it almost exclusively affects males.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Females are the carriers; affected men pass the gene to all their daughters but none of their sons.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The factor VIII gene lies on the X chromosome, and inheritance is X-linked recessive.

questions.pearl: Haemophilia: prolonged APTT with normal PT and bleeding time; presents with haemarthroses and muscle haematomas.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Cystic hygroma is a lateral swelling, usually in the posterior triangle, brilliantly transilluminant.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The subhyoid bursa lies in the midline below the hyoid and can enlarge to present as a midline swelling.

options.label: C
options.explanation: A plunging ranula extends through the mylohyoid into the submental region, presenting as a midline swelling in the upper neck.

options.label: D
options.explanation: A branchial cyst lies laterally, deep to the anterior border of sternocleidomastoid.

questions.pearl: A midline swelling that moves on swallowing and with tongue protrusion is a thyroglossal cyst; one that moves only on swallowing is thyroid.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Splenomegaly is a feature of CML; a leukaemoid reaction usually has no or minimal splenomegaly.

options.label: B
options.explanation: WBC count exceeds 50,000/µL as a reactive response to infection, haemorrhage or malignancy.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Platelets are usually normal, unlike the thrombocytosis or later thrombocytopenia of CML.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Toxic granulation and Döhle bodies in neutrophils reflect reactive (infective) leukocytosis.

questions.pearl: Leukaemoid reaction has a high neutrophil alkaline phosphatase (NAP) score; CML has a low NAP score and the Philadelphia chromosome.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Skin contains drug-metabolising enzymes (cytochrome P450, conjugating enzymes) and is a minor extrahepatic site of metabolism.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The liver is the main site of drug metabolism through phase I (CYP450) and phase II (conjugation) reactions.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The kidney metabolises some drugs; for example, renal dehydropeptidase breaks down imipenem, hence it is given with cilastatin.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Teeth have no metabolic role for drugs, though tetracyclines are deposited in them.

questions.pearl: Imipenem is co-administered with cilastatin to block renal dehydropeptidase-I and prevent its renal inactivation.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: DVT may cause a low-grade fever only; high fever suggests cellulitis or another infection.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Sensation is preserved in DVT; sensory loss suggests arterial ischaemia or neuropathy.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Unilateral calf or whole-leg swelling (calf circumference difference over 3 cm) is the commonest sign.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Venous obstruction causes pitting oedema (a Wells criterion); non-pitting oedema suggests lymphoedema (filariasis, Milroy disease) or myxoedema.

questions.pearl: Wells score guides DVT workup: low probability plus negative D-dimer excludes DVT; otherwise do compression ultrasound.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Arterial stiffening with age raises systolic BP; isolated systolic hypertension is common in the elderly.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Type 1 diabetes is autoimmune and usually starts in childhood or adolescence.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Senile cataract is the commonest cause of reversible blindness and rises steeply with age.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Benign prostatic hyperplasia is present histologically in most men over 60.

questions.pearl: Age is the single biggest risk factor for cataract, BPH, osteoarthritis, osteoporosis and most cancers.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: EBV is linked to Burkitt lymphoma, nasopharyngeal carcinoma and Hodgkin lymphoma.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Cytomegalovirus is classed among the potentially oncogenic herpesviruses in standard microbiology texts, with transforming ability in vitro.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Chronic HBV infection, with viral DNA integration, is a leading cause of hepatocellular carcinoma.

options.label: D
options.explanation: HIV is not directly oncogenic; AIDS-related cancers arise from immunosuppression and co-infection (HHV-8, EBV, HPV).

questions.pearl: Oncogenic viruses: EBV, HPV 16/18, HBV, HCV, HHV-8 (Kaposi sarcoma), HTLV-1 (adult T-cell leukaemia), Merkel cell polyomavirus.

questions.subject: Specialized Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Calcium oxalate (alone or mixed with phosphate) forms about 75–80% of renal stones; they are radio-opaque.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Pure calcium phosphate stones are less common and associated with renal tubular acidosis.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Xanthine stones are rare, seen in xanthine oxidase deficiency or with allopurinol.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Uric acid stones form about 5–10% and are radiolucent.

questions.pearl: Radiolucent stones: uric acid, xanthine and indinavir; cystine stones are faintly opaque; struvite forms staghorn calculi in urease infections.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Heat-stable enterotoxins (A–E) cause vomiting 1–6 hours after ingestion.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Staph. aureus, along with Streptococcus pyogenes, causes skin and soft tissue infection including cellulitis.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Staphylococcal pneumonia follows influenza and causes cavitation, pneumatoceles and empyema.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Exfoliative toxin causes staphylococcal scalded skin syndrome (Ritter's disease), which resembles toxic epidermal necrolysis.

questions.pearl: SSSS splits the epidermis at the granular layer (intraepidermal, Nikolsky positive) and spares mucosa; drug-induced TEN splits at the dermo-epidermal junction.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: The surgeon cannot palpate tissues directly, so haptic feedback is lost.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Smaller wounds mean fewer wound infections than open surgery; this is an advantage.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Controlling major bleeding is harder through ports and may require conversion to open surgery.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Large specimens are difficult to remove and need bag extraction, morcellation or a wound extension.

questions.pearl: Laparoscopy also has a two-dimensional view and pneumoperitoneum effects (raised intra-abdominal pressure, CO2 absorption, gas embolism).

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: The kidney is the main route of drug excretion through glomerular filtration and tubular secretion.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Large polar molecules and conjugates are excreted in bile and some undergo enterohepatic circulation.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Volatile anaesthetics and alcohol are excreted in expired air.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The liver is the principal organ of drug metabolism; it excretes via bile, which is counted as a separate route.

questions.pearl: Other excretion routes: saliva, sweat, milk (important in lactation) and faeces.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Reduced LDL-receptor expression lowers LDL clearance; check TSH in every patient with raised cholesterol.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Oestrogen and progesterone raise cholesterol and triglycerides physiologically in pregnancy.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Fibrates are PPAR-alpha agonists used to lower triglycerides; they do not raise cholesterol.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Hypoparathyroidism causes hypocalcaemia and is not a recognised cause of hypercholesterolaemia.

questions.pearl: Secondary hyperlipidaemia: hypothyroidism, nephrotic syndrome, diabetes, cholestasis, obesity, alcohol, thiazides, steroids.

questions.subject: Pediatrics

options.label: A
options.explanation: ASD is not a component; its addition makes 'pentalogy of Fallot'.

options.label: B
options.explanation: A large malaligned perimembranous VSD is a core component.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The aorta overrides the VSD and receives blood from both ventricles.

options.label: D
options.explanation: TOF has pulmonary (infundibular) stenosis with reduced pulmonary flow, not pulmonary hypertension.

questions.pearl: TOF: VSD, pulmonary stenosis, overriding aorta, right ventricular hypertrophy; CXR shows a boot-shaped heart with oligaemic lungs.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Nasal retinal fibres decussate at the chiasma; compression causes bitemporal hemianopia.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The medial geniculate body relays auditory pathways; vision relays in the lateral geniculate body.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Optic radiations carry fibres from the lateral geniculate body to the occipital cortex.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The oculomotor nerve is efferent to eye muscles and pupil; it is not part of the afferent visual pathway.

questions.pearl: Visual pathway: optic nerve → chiasma → optic tract → lateral geniculate body → optic radiation → visual cortex (area 17).

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Normal red cells are biconcave, which maximises surface area for gas exchange and deformability.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Mature human red cells are anuclear, leaving more room for haemoglobin.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Tear drop cells (dacrocytes) are abnormal and suggest myelofibrosis or marrow infiltration.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Red cells are discs about 7.5 µm in diameter with central pallor occupying about one-third.

questions.pearl: Spherocytes lose their central pallor and biconcavity; they are seen in hereditary spherocytosis and autoimmune haemolysis.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Calcium gluconate stabilises the myocardium in hyperkalaemia; it does not raise potassium.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Glucose stimulates insulin release and drives K+ into cells, which would worsen hypokalaemia.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Replacement with oral or IV potassium chloride is the treatment; IV rate normally not above 10–20 mmol/h.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Calcium resonium removes potassium from the gut and is used for hyperkalaemia.

questions.pearl: Refractory hypokalaemia: check and correct magnesium, as hypomagnesaemia causes renal potassium wasting.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Septic arthritis is the most important cause to exclude in an acute hot swollen joint; aspirate before antibiotics.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Acute gout typically affects a single joint, classically the first metatarsophalangeal joint (podagra).

options.label: C
options.explanation: TB causes a chronic monoarthritis of large weight-bearing joints such as hip and knee.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Psoriatic arthritis is usually an asymmetrical oligo- or polyarthritis with DIP involvement and dactylitis, rather than a classic monoarthritis.

questions.pearl: Acute monoarthritis = septic arthritis until proven otherwise; joint aspiration for Gram stain, culture and crystals is mandatory.

questions.subject: Gynecology
questions.stem: Causes (risk factors) of ruptured ectopic pregnancy:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Tubal damage from PID or prior surgery impairs ovum transport, the main risk factor for tubal pregnancy.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Failed sterilisation carries a high proportion of ectopic pregnancies due to recanalisation or fistula.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Peritubal adhesions and tubal distortion from endometriosis increase ectopic risk.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Parity itself is not a risk factor; previous ectopic, PID, IVF and IUCD failure are.

questions.pearl: Isthmic tubal pregnancies rupture earliest (6–8 weeks); interstitial ones rupture late with catastrophic bleeding.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Polyps block odorants from reaching the olfactory cleft, causing conductive anosmia.

options.label: B
options.explanation: A severe septal deviation obstructs airflow to the olfactory area, causing conductive hyposmia or anosmia.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Mucosal oedema in allergic rhinitis reduces olfactory airflow.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Olfactory groove meningioma, frontal lobe tumours and head injury cause sensorineural anosmia.

questions.pearl: Unilateral anosmia with personality change suggests olfactory groove meningioma (Foster Kennedy syndrome if with optic atrophy and papilloedema).

questions.subject: Pediatrics

options.label: A
options.explanation: Bilateral pitting oedema of nutritional origin is diagnostic of SAM by itself.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The criterion is a weight-for-height Z score below -3 SD.

options.label: C
options.explanation: MUAC below 115 mm defines SAM; 115–124 mm indicates moderate acute malnutrition.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Anaemia is a common complication of SAM but not a diagnostic criterion.

questions.pearl: SAM with complications (oedema, poor appetite, medical illness) needs inpatient care; uncomplicated SAM can be managed with RUTF in the community.

questions.subject: Specialized Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Ureteric colic radiates from loin to groin, scrotum or labia, following the T11–L1 dermatomes.

options.label: B
options.text: Pain is associated with stone size
options.explanation: Pain severity does not correlate with stone size; small stones causing acute obstruction are often most painful.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Low fluid intake and diets high in animal protein, salt and oxalate increase stone formation.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Stones cause painful haematuria; painless haematuria suggests urothelial malignancy until proven otherwise.

questions.pearl: Stones under 5 mm usually pass spontaneously; tamsulosin aids passage of distal ureteric stones.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.stem: Posterior segment structures of the eye:

options.label: A
options.explanation: The vitreous fills the posterior segment behind the lens.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The lens lies in the anterior segment, behind the iris, separating the anterior and posterior segments.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The choroid is the vascular layer of the posterior uvea between retina and sclera.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The retina lines the posterior segment as the neurosensory layer.

questions.pearl: Anterior segment: cornea, anterior and posterior chambers, iris, ciliary body, lens; posterior segment: vitreous, retina, choroid, optic disc.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: Major criteria of acute rheumatic fever:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Arthralgia is a minor criterion and cannot be counted if arthritis is used as a major one.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Sydenham's chorea is a major criterion.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Raised CRP or ESR is a minor criterion.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Painless subcutaneous nodules over bony prominences and tendons are a major criterion, usually with carditis.

questions.pearl: Diagnosis requires evidence of preceding streptococcal infection plus 2 major, or 1 major and 2 minor, criteria.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.stem: Causes of gradual dimness of vision:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Progressive lens opacity causes gradual painless loss of vision.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Age-related loss of accommodation gradually impairs near vision after about 40 years.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Absolute glaucoma is the end stage with no perception of light; there is no remaining vision to dim.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Vitamin A deficiency causes progressive night blindness and xerophthalmia.

questions.pearl: Gradual painless loss: cataract, refractive error, chronic open-angle glaucoma, diabetic retinopathy, ARMD.

questions.subject: Gynecology

options.label: A
options.explanation: Endometrial glands within the myometrium enlarge the uterus and cause heavy, painful periods.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Submucous and intramural fibroids increase endometrial surface area and impair contraction, causing menorrhagia.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Carcinoma cervix causes irregular, postcoital or intermenstrual bleeding rather than heavy regular periods.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Cervical polyps cause intermenstrual or contact bleeding, not menorrhagia.

questions.pearl: PALM-COEIN classification of AUB: Polyp, Adenomyosis, Leiomyoma, Malignancy; Coagulopathy, Ovulatory, Endometrial, Iatrogenic, Not classified.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Chronic lymphocytic leukaemia causes painless symmetrical generalised lymphadenopathy in the elderly.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Disseminated TB can cause generalised lymphadenopathy, though cervical nodes are most commonly involved.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Indian kala-azar causes massive splenomegaly and hepatomegaly; lymphadenopathy is uncommon (more typical of African disease).

options.label: D
options.explanation: Secondary syphilis produces generalised, painless, rubbery lymphadenopathy with rash and mucous patches.

questions.pearl: Generalised lymphadenopathy: infections (HIV, TB, EBV, syphilis), lymphoma, CLL/ALL, SLE, sarcoidosis, drugs (phenytoin).

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Steroids reduce trabecular outflow, causing steroid-induced open-angle glaucoma in susceptible people.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Long-term steroids cause posterior subcapsular cataract.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Steroids suppress corneal neovascularisation and are used to treat it.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Steroids do not cause miosis; they may cause mild mydriasis and ptosis.

questions.pearl: Topical steroids are contraindicated in herpes simplex dendritic ulcer — they can cause geographic ulcer and perforation.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.stem: Cataract is a frequent complication of:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Leprosy causes lagophthalmos, corneal anaesthesia and iridocyclitis; cataract is not a frequent direct complication.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Myotonic dystrophy classically causes a 'Christmas tree' polychromatic cataract.

options.label: C
options.explanation: TB causes uveitis and choroidal tubercles; cataract is not a frequent complication.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Acute angle closure may leave small anterior subcapsular opacities (glaukomflecken), but cataract is not a frequent complication.

questions.pearl: Systemic causes of cataract: diabetes, galactosaemia, hypocalcaemia, Wilson's (sunflower), myotonic dystrophy, Down syndrome, steroids.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.stem: Prophylactic antibiotics are given in which surgeries:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Ischaemic tissue risks clostridial gas gangrene, so prophylaxis (e.g. benzylpenicillin or co-amoxiclav) is recommended for lower limb amputation.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Routine clean surgery without implant does not need prophylaxis; it is given when a prosthesis or implant is inserted.

options.label: C
options.text: Clean inguinal hernia repair without mesh
options.explanation: Clean surgery with no implant and low infection risk does not require prophylaxis.

options.label: D
options.explanation: A ruptured appendix is dirty surgery needing therapeutic antibiotics covering gut aerobes and anaerobes.

questions.pearl: Prophylaxis is given at induction (within 60 minutes of incision) and usually no more than one dose.

questions.subject: Obstetrics

options.label: A
options.explanation: Fetal hyperglycaemia causes osmotic diuresis and polyhydramnios, not oligohydramnios.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Poor glycaemic control is associated with unexplained late stillbirth.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Anomalies arise when hyperglycaemia is present in the first trimester, as in undiagnosed pre-existing diabetes.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Fetal hyperinsulinaemia (Pedersen hypothesis) drives growth, causing macrosomia and shoulder dystocia.

questions.pearl: Neonatal problems in GDM: hypoglycaemia, respiratory distress, hypocalcaemia, polycythaemia, jaundice.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Dengue is a flavivirus transmitted by Aedes aegypti, a day-biting mosquito.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Yellow fever is a flavivirus transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Chikungunya is an alphavirus spread by Aedes, causing fever with severe arthralgia.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Malaria is mosquito-borne (Anopheles) but caused by a protozoan parasite, Plasmodium, not a virus.

questions.pearl: Aedes transmits dengue, chikungunya, yellow fever and Zika; Culex transmits Japanese encephalitis and filariasis; Anopheles transmits malaria.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Globe perforation is an anaesthetic or operative (peribulbar needle) complication, not a post-operative one.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Post-operative inflammation (anterior uveitis) is common and treated with topical steroids.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Expulsive suprachoroidal haemorrhage is a rare but devastating intraoperative complication.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Retained viscoelastic, inflammation or pupillary block can raise IOP after surgery (secondary glaucoma).

questions.pearl: Commonest late complication after cataract surgery is posterior capsular opacification, treated with Nd:YAG laser capsulotomy.
